title: StrictRoosModel
statement: Let A be an abelian category with countable products. For a cochain complex X of strict towers (functors from the opposite natural-number order to A), write X_n for its evaluated complex and t_n:X_(n+1)→X_n for its transition. Put P(X)=∏_n X_n and let u(X):P(X)→P(X) have nth component π_n−π_(n+1)t_n [def-weil-tower-transition-endomorphism]. Define F(X)=Cone(u(X))[-1] [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For a strict morphism f:X→Y, define F(f) by the shifted cone map induced by ∏_n f_n on both products. The canonical shift and cone coordinates, followed by the biproduct braiding, identify F(X)^(p+1) with P(X)^p⊕P(X)^(p+1). In these coordinates the differential is (y,z)↦(−dy−u(z),dz), maps are diagonal product maps, and evaluation at n is the second projection followed by π_n. If A also has tower limits, define the inclusion lim X_n→F(X) by coordinates (0,(π_n)_n). For any compatible family γ_n:P→X_n, define its strict augmentation P→F(X) by coordinates (0,(γ_n)_n), and its ordinary-limit lift by the limit universal property. These are explicit constructions, natural in strict tower maps. When the derived categories exist, localizing this inclusion and composing with a descent factorization κ defines the natural transformation roosDerivedUnit κ. The module-sheaf context is the specialization of these constructions to [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

proof.text: Construct products and 1-s, use strict naturality to define the cone functor, shift by -1, and use canonical shift and biproduct isomorphisms. The mapping-cocone lift defines the limit inclusion and augmentations. Verify all equations coordinatewise.
